answer: Payouts can price substitutes rather than detect them. Submissions are drawn into random packets of eight, graded as packets. A key earns the average packet-score drop caused by deleting its entry. A thousand copies are interchangeable: delete one and the packet is unchanged, so the family gets one share. N shares take N entries whose removal each hurts: N different pieces of work. No similarity scan, no ban; counterfactual packets are public, so the arithmetic replays. A claim's horizon is one epoch; unclaimed shares return to the common haven, and the opal is quality, not key count.
